title: Client telemetry & streaming handshake prioritization rubric
creator: Ava Chen
description: This ticket captures a pragmatic triage rubric and decision record for incoming enterprise SDK/client library feature requests that affect streaming ergonomics, authentication patterns, and telemetry/observability. Goal: provide a fast, repeatable intake path so PMs and ENG/SEC can score requests consistently, produce actionable prioritization, and feed the roadmap for SDK parity across languages without duplicating ad-hoc debates per customer.
acceptance_criteria: A documented rubric (scoring sheet) that covers Impact, Engineering Effort, Security Risk, Backwards Compatibility, and Strategic Alignment
A short list (<= 6) of prioritized SDK changes for Q2 driven by customer signals and rubric scores
Owner assignments for follow-up discovery or RFCs and dates for decision gates
Signoff from Security on auth pattern recommendations before engineering work begins
triage_matrix: Scoring columns: Impact (0-5), Effort (0-5, lower is better), Security Risk (0-5), Enterprise Priority (0-5), Net Score = Impact + Enterprise Priority - Effort - Security Risk
Interpretation: Net Score >= 4 -> Candidate for next sprint planning; 1-3 -> Needs more discovery or design; <=0 -> Defer or require executive escalation
Qualifiers: If Security Risk >=4, require security review and threat model before scheduling regardless of net score
Impact definition: considers number of paying customers affected, SLAs, and revenue/contract exposure
Effort definition: rough cross-functional points including SDK implementation, test matrix, docs, sample apps, and downstream runtime/runtime compatibility
sample_requests: Customer: FinTechX — Request: resumable streaming connections for unreliable mobile networks + token rotation without breaking in-flight streams; initial ask: language SDKs (python, js) — Notes: contractual uptime clause, high revenue exposure

Customer: SearchCorp — Request: richer client-side telemetry (per-request token usage, latency histograms, streaming chunk sizes) surfaced to Console with sampling control; medium revenue but high developer experience importance
Customer: HealthSys — Request: PKCS11/HSM-support SDK hooks and server-to-server mTLS examples for on-prem private deployment; compliance-bound, requires audit trail

Customer: RetailAI — Request: simplified streaming ergonomics in JS SDK (async iterator + reconnect/backoff built-in) with transparent auth refresh — broad adoption potential, low incremental revenue immediate
decision: After workshop (2026-03-05) we prioritized three tracks: 1) Auth resiliency for streaming (resumable streams + token rotation) as high priority (Net Score 5) due to multiple enterprise contracts; 2) Console telemetry export format + sampling control as medium-high priority (Net Score 3) to unblock long-term observability features; 3) Language ergonomics for JS (async iterator + inline reconnect) as medium priority (Net Score 2) to be scheduled after auth/resiliency work. HSM/PKCS11 examples require security/legal signoff and are tracked as discovery-only for now.

comments: 2026-03-02 Ava Chen: Created initial ticket after customer intake calls (FinTechX, RetailAI, HealthSys). Observed repeated asks around auth and streaming resiliency — pattern fits enterprise SLA risk.

2026-03-04 Priya Nair: Security flagged that token rotation during an active stream is a non-trivial PKI problem; suggested we evaluate re-auth handshake patterns vs in-band refresh tokens. Security review will be required for any approach that stores secrets in memory for reconnects.

2026-03-05 Diego Martinez: Ran triage workshop with Eng (runtime, SDK), Design, Security, and Solutions. Captured scoring rubric and tested it on 4 incoming requests. Consensus: implement resumable streams with short-lived reconnect tokens and server-side session recovery as first path.

2026-03-07 Mateo Ruiz: Design note — JS ergonomics can be implemented as thin wrapper on top of core streaming primitives; recommend decoupling API ergonomics work from auth/rehydration logic to reduce risk and unblock parallel work.
2026-03-10 Ava Chen: Noted that SearchCorp telemetry ask lines up with Console roadmap (trace-level linking). Flagging as candidate for cross-team sync during Console planning meeting.

2026-03-12 Priya Nair: Security review kick-off scheduled. Primary concerns: replay attacks during reconnect, token leakage in logs, and compatibility with customer HSMs. Action: deliver threat model by 2026-03-20.

2026-03-14 Diego Martinez: Spikes greenlit. Prototype scope: a) server session token that can resume with proof-of-possession, b) client SDK pattern for token hot-swap without dropping message boundaries. ETA for triage demo: 2026-03-21. Assigning follow-ups in ENG board.
